lines: A 3HP blank strip that carries a line of your own text down its face, for naming a group of modules; it has no jacks and passes no signal
Note — the strip does nothing until you right-click it and type into the text field in its menu; until then it reads Rt-click to edit
Note — the text is written in white, sideways, and reading upwards from the bottom of the panel; long text breaks onto a second line on its own
Note — the text is saved in the patch, and shows as Your message here! in the module browser
Menu — Edit this strip's label: — the heading over a text field; type the strip's text there and press Enter, which sets it and closes the menu
Menu — Flip text top-to-bottom — turns the text the other way up so it reads downwards from the top of the panel
ScribbleStrip.notes: Open source, read at commit 4a148ff, whose plugin.json is byte-identical to the installed 2.0.1 build; that is the last commit on the repository and the only one carrying version 2.0.1. The module has no parameters, no inputs, no outputs and no lights, and its process() body is empty, so nothing here can be tagged. The text field in the menu takes the keyboard for as long as the menu is open: EventParamField::step calls setSelectedWidget on itself every frame. Enter commits; dismissing the menu any other way leaves the old text. There is no undo entry for a text change, since the module writes the string directly rather than through a history action. The typeface is Mad Midnight Marker by Darrell Flood, shipped in res/. The README's two screenshots are current.
